text:
alex_cs: Received escalation from ACME. They have a Dedicated EU pool pinned to eu-west-1 but ~7% of requests are being served from hosted us-east-1 after ~1h of steady traffic. Customer reports latency spike (avg 300ms -> 1.2s) and unexpected hosted billing. Repro steps + snippets below.

nina_eng: Can you paste the exact pin config and any autoscale events around the time?

alex_cs: Config they shared:
```yaml
region_pin: eu-west-1
pin_ttl_seconds: 3600
fallback: hosted-global
pool_id: ded-eu-42
```
Customer curl they ran (sanitized):
```bash
for i in {1..100}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \\  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -w "%{http_code} %{time_starttransfer}\n"
done
```
Logs from their responses show: `X-Served-From: hosted-us-east-1` for ~7 requests, and the response times there ~1.0-1.3s. A few responses returned 403 for tool calls around the same time.

kai_sre: Looking at our routing logs for pool ded-eu-42: pin created at 1767438200 with ttl=3600s. At 1767441805 there's a cache eviction entry and the route fell back to hosted. I can see a pattern: when the dedicated pool was scaled down and reattached, the pin metadata wasn't re-registered.

jess_pm: Is this specific to geo pins or all dedicated pins? Any customer-facing config that might trigger TTL expiry earlier?

nina_eng: Preliminary hypothesis: autoscaler replaced a node instance which cleared in-memory pin registration. The pin TTL should be refreshed on pool lifecycle events, but the refresh hook wasn't firing during scale-down->up path. That leads to routing cache miss and fallback to hosted.

alex_cs: Customer also pasted a snippet of their admin events showing a manual scale change at 1767441750 (they did a small scale down to mitigate latency).

nina_eng: Repro steps I'm going to run in staging: 1) create dedicated pool with region_pin eu-west-1 and ttl=3600 2) warm with 200 concurrent requests 3) trigger scale down (-1) then scale up (+1) 4) observe routing header in responses. We'll use the same curl loop.

kai_sre: I'll try to reproduce as well. If confirmed, mitigation: temporarily increase pin_ttl_seconds to 43200 (12h) for affected customers and push a routing policy override to prefer dedicated for pinned customers while we patch.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Started canary deployment of fix branch `ttl-refresh-fix` to staging (release 2026.3.19-canary).

billing-bot: billing-bot: Notified billing ops. If confirmed, prepare customer credit for tokens billed to hosted pool during the window.

nina_eng: Created tracker RWINF-893. Root cause: pin metadata not persisted across pool lifecycle transitions due to race in the pool-manager -> pin-registry handshake (missing ack). PR #2714 opened to add explicit re-register on pool attach + unit tests. ETA for prod patch: 3 hours after canary validation.

alex_cs: Great — I'll send the customer a concise update: repro, immediate mitigations (increase TTL or routing override), and that billing will be reviewed/credited.

kai_sre: Confirmed repro on staging: scale down + up leads to ~5-8% requests hitting hosted fallback when heavy concurrency present. Canary looks good so far; will monitor for next 30m then schedule prod patch.

alex_cs: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the customer and close the loop once billing credit is posted. :thumbsup:
